Stardew Valley is a game about farming look like harvest moon, but there are more adventures awaiting curious players beyond cultivating a rich and bountiful garden. From mining and fishing to making friends and falling in love, Stardew Valley's Pelican Town is stuffed with rewarding opportunities. As modern day woes give way to pressing matters on the farm and within your newfound community, Stardew Valley's meditative activities often lead to personal reflection in the real world. It’s a game that tugs at your curiousity as often as it does your heart. This game recomended and funniest to play.

Recommended to play 5/5

seems like a simple pixel farming game, but hides many secrets and twists. I love this game because you have free choice to do whatever you want and are not forced to progress a particular quest or skill. After many years, this game is still well loved and I find myself coming back again and again to play another run as there are many options and long-term goals that make the single and co-op experience different each time.

Super fun and relaxing game to play, has some story and interesting characters to keep it interesting on top of the typical farming mechanics. But nothing too serious or depressing to distract from the fun game play, plus the nice pixel art and music are nice touches. Highly recommend~

10/10. I bought this thinking I’d casually farm, make some money, and maybe romance a cute villager.

Instead, I am emotionally attached to pixel people, checking the weather like it affects my real life, reorganizing my farm at 2AM, hoarding random items because “I might need this later,” and beefing with Pierre.

There is ALWAYS something to do, but somehow it never feels stressful unless you make it stressful. You can farm, fish, mine, decorate, raise animals, make friends, get married, ignore everyone and become a cave-dwelling millionaire… whatever makes you happy.

It’s one of those games where you sit down to play for “like an hour” and suddenly an entire season has passed and you have no idea what happened to your evening.

Extremely cozy. Extremely addictive. Concerned Ape basically sold me a second life for the price of a game.

Would recommend. 🌱🐓💗

I've had this game since it first released back in 2016, and I still play it to this day. Honestly it's my favorite game, hands down. Best part about it, this game was being sold for $10 when I first got it, the price has gone up since then, and justifiably so. It's honestly worth the money, you never run out of things to do. I mean I guess there is 100% completion, but even after that there are still mods that can expand the game, Stardew Valley is decently mod-friendly. I recommend Nexus Mods if you're looking to mod the game. If you decide you are not for mods, then you can still farm, fish, and interact with the NPCs even on 100% completion, and the events are still there too. Plus, to add to it, they made it multiplayer back in 2017, a year after they first launched the game. I have never played a game with a more dedicated community, or a dedicated game developer such as this one. 10/10 would recommend!

(edit of my review to add) It's been nearly 10 years since I first booted Stardew Valley. The more time I spend in the game, and the more updates that have come out, the more I have loved Stardew. The creator, CA, is an absolute treasure and anything he makes or touches must be protected at all costs. The mods are super fun, the updates are large (and free?!), and it's still just as charming as the first time I booted it. Stardew will forever have a very special place in my heart. I'm still making discoveries and learning new things, even with my xbox save being Winter Y8!

This game quickly sucked me into a black hole of nonstop farming once I began playing. Even though you may get tired of it and take a break for a month, it STILL somehow manages to make you addicted for another 2 weeks.

I admire the charm, story, and the different objectives that you can complete. Compared to other farming games, the story itself with the cute apple ghosts as well as the cute farm animals provide a continuous obligation to please them.

Even if you're a systematic person that doesn't care for cuteness, you can personalize your farm to look as if a machine plopped your crops onto your land.

All in all:
Pros: charming, addictive, good storyline, easy to learn mechanics
Cons: pixel art style may not be the best for everyone, you may forget to water your plants irl because you're too addicted to the game
